I remember the first time I fully grasped the implications of Goedel’s Incompleteness Theorem. It was a rough week for me. I actually had my world view significantly altered and I felt very depressed because it seemed as though some sort of goal of humankind had been rendered well-and-truly unreachable.

The ELI5 version is, “oh my god, where are your parents?!”

J/k, basically Goedel’s Incompleteness Theorem is a way to prove that any system of math powerful enough to be useful will call “false” on a statement that is true. Effectively, it demonstrates that there is no such system that can ever be created that will precisely recognize all true things as “true” and all false things as “false”. There is a fairly simple way that any logical system (that is powerful enough to be useful) can be made to contradict itself.

It may seem silly to get so torn up about math, but Principia Mathematica was a valiant effort by many smart people to overcome this fact. I would not be surprised to learn of a suicide or two from people back in the day when Goedel’s paper was published.
